name: Thasunda Brown Duckett

career.title: Director of Emerging Markets (affordable housing and homeownership initiatives)
Home lending roles, incl. National Retail Sales Executive, Chase Mortgage Banking

background_rationale: Built her career in consumer-facing lending and banking, from Fannie Mae emerging-markets outreach to running mortgage retail sales, Chase Auto Finance and Chase Consumer Banking.

notable.summary: TIAA completed the sale of TIAA Bank to a group of private investment firms, with the bank resuming the EverBank name.
TIAA reported that its RetirePlus lifetime-income default offering had surpassed 400,000 participant accounts and $30 billion in assets.
In a CNBC Changemakers profile, Duckett said that by being herself in corporate spaces she can "continue to put cracks in the ceiling for the next generation of leaders."
TIAA announced a strategic partnership with Accenture to modernize retirement recordkeeping starting in 2025, with about 1,500 TIAA employees in the U.S. and India moving to Accenture.

personal_story.hook: Thasunda Brown Duckett had to tell her father his pension wasn't enough; she now runs a retirement giant.
personal_story.summary: Duckett was born in Rochester, New York; her father worked in a Xerox warehouse before losing his job and moving the family to Texas, and her mother was a teacher. She has said she knows what it is like to open the refrigerator and see only baking soda, or to have the lights turned off. At the University of Houston she interned at Fannie Mae and, after graduating, took its offer even though it was the lowest she received, because she knew the company and its people. She spent 17 years at JPMorgan Chase, rising to run Chase Auto Finance and then Chase Consumer Banking, before becoming TIAA's CEO in 2021.
